identity.name: STAR HEALTH & AL INS CO L
identity.industry: Standalone Health Insurance (SAHI) — retail-health-led general insurer

summary.oneLiner: which management attributes partly to long-term-policy reporting optics and partly to an explicit refusal to chase "riskier pools". The two open questions the call did not close: management **explicitly refuses to guide on loss ratio**, and the GST-waiver demand tailwind enters its own base in H2 FY27.

one-line thesis: The turnaround is now four quarters old and compounding: underwriting result swung to Rs 111 crore vs Rs 16 crore a year ago, the Combined Insurance Service Ratio improved 1.7% from 98.7% to 97%, and normalised PAT rose 44% YoY to Rs 386 crore with annualised ROE up from 12.2% to 15.6%. Growth is deliberately quality-led rather than share-led — GWP +19% and fresh retail health GWP +37% (1/N) with 94% of fresh retail business new-to-insurance, but retail market share slipped 31% → 29%, which management attributes partly to long-term-policy reporting optics and partly to an explicit refusal to chase "riskier pools". The two open questions the call did not close: management explicitly refuses to guide on loss ratio, and the GST-waiver demand tailwind enters its own base in H2 FY27.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > All figures as management stated them on the call. Reporting basis is Ind AS ("We report our statutory financials on Ind AS basis, following the regulator's guidelines on Ind AS transition"), and business numbers are given on both 1/N (reported) and N basis — do not mix the two across quarters.
> One-offs / distortions to call out explicitly:

> 1. 1/N vs N reporting. Long-term (multi-year) policies distort every top-line comparison. Management: "clean like-for-like comparability will be restored only by FY28." Long-term is "closer to about 40% of fresh" on the retail side.
> 2. Normalised PAT is a management construct, not a statutory number — Rs 386 crore (normalised) vs Rs 550 crore (reported); the wedge is investment mark-to-market against an assumed 8% yield.
> 3. GST input tax credit withdrawal inflates the opex line ~20% YoY — a base effect, not a run-rate deterioration.

> 4. Group-book shrinkage flatters the blended loss ratio. Group was ~5% of GWP in Q1 FY26, "now it looks closer to 2.5%"; COO: "there is some component of that, but we've seen an improvement in the retail loss ratio also."
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Insurance revenue growth: "We believe it should start touching 15-16% as we keep on moving ahead through the quarters" and "we will see a 15-16% growth going forward throughout the year. It will keep on increasing in FY28 as well." (vs 13.4% this quarter.)
Expense ratio: "30-40 basis points improvement in the expense ratio is something which we'll get consistently over the years."

Loss ratio — NO GUIDANCE, explicitly. CEO corrected an analyst who read the 30-40 bps as a loss-ratio number: "the comment made by Nilesh was not about loss ratio improvement. It was about expense ratio improvement... We are not giving any guidance for loss ratio improvement."
ROE: "all the efforts that the organisation is taking is to deliver a mid- to high-teen ROE... We don't want to give any number in particular, but that is the glide path."
Reinsurance cost: net reinsurance expense was "around 0.9 percentage points" in FY26; for FY27-28 "very difficult to comment at this moment, but it should be in the range of 0.5%, 0.6%."
Q2 loss-ratio seasonality: "Q2 generally is a higher loss ratio for health insurance business as you are aware. So, we expect the same trends to continue this year as well."

H2 growth moderation: post the GST waiver "there was a significant jump in the growth rates for the entire industry and for us as well in H2 of last year. So, some moderation in growth rates which will happen... the growth rate optically may definitely moderate for everyone including for Star Health."
order book & pipeline: Not applicable to an insurer — the equivalent forward-book indicators management gave:
Renewal ratio 102%, up 3% YoY — the in-force book is self-renewing above 100% (premium-weighted).
Fresh : renewal mix ~20 : 80 of insurance revenue.

Long-term (multi-year) policies ≈ 40% of fresh retail — premium already collected but recognised over "a 2-3 year period", i.e. a contracted revenue backlog that supports the guided step-up from 13.4% to 15-16%.
8.5 lakh agents after adding "around 20,000 new agents during this quarter", with agent productivity +19% YoY.
segment / subsidiary detail: Retail health — the franchise. Loss ratio "closer to 67.5% to 68%". Fresh retail health GWP +37% YoY (1/N). New-to-insurance mix on fresh retail 94% vs 90% in Q1 FY26.

Group / corporate — deliberately shrunk: ~5% of GWP in Q1 FY26 → "closer to 2.5%" now. "Within the corporate groups, SME business through agency remains the priority." Part of the YoY loss-ratio improvement comes from group.
Senior citizens — "hardly under 5% now of the overall book. We largely focused on younger cohorts of consumers." (Material mix change for a company historically identified with senior-citizen cover.)

Distribution: proprietary channels (agency + digital D2C) = 90%+ of overall retail business. Within digital, 74% of fresh business originates from own D2C; D2C fresh business +142% YoY with 98% of customers new to insurance. Bancassurance/partnerships/alternate are explicitly secondary.
Geography: "Fresh business growth from non-metro geographies is 3.5 times that of growth in the metro geographies."
Investments: investment income Rs 644 crore, +10% YoY; CIO on the call but no portfolio breakdown given.
growth verticals / optionality: Category expansion via GST waiver — "The impact of enhanced affordability due to the GST waiver is very evident through category growth, with majority of our fresh business emerging from first-time buyers."
Digital D2C — "our fastest growing profitable channel", +142% YoY fresh, and the lowest cost-to-acquire leg of the 90%+ proprietary mix.

Wellness / telemedicine / home healthcare as a loss-ratio lever — "extending our ability to manage fever and infection-related cases very efficiently"; COO: "huge scale-up has been achieved quarter to quarter."

Generative AI on claims — "we are in the process of layering generative AI over and above our existing AI/ML analytical layers to drive greater precision of claims operations"; AI/ML already "showing encouraging results with respect to mitigation of fraud, waste and abuse."
Customer app — "~16 million downloads and over 1.5 million monthly active users", with self-service renewals/claims/service requests building.
Regulatory-reform optionality — a commission/distribution reform would land on a book already 90% proprietary (see §6a).
6a. moat & competitive position: Twenty years of longitudinal claims data. "Our greatest advantage is the proprietary data we have built over the last 20 years. This is a unique asset that is difficult to replicate and provides a significant competitive advantage." Scale evidence: "helping more than 2.8 crore lives during these last 20 years"; ~19,000 employees — "Star Health is probably also the largest employer in the entire General Insurance space, even while counting public sector companies."

Proprietary distribution as a structural cost/selection edge. "Our proprietary channels... contributed 90% plus of overall retail business. This proprietary distribution gives us leverage over customer selection, quality of sales and economics of acquisition." 8.5 lakh agents with productivity +19% YoY.

Regulatory headroom on expenses vs peers. "Star Health is probably the only company in the SAHI space which is already operating within the expense of management limits set out by the regulator and we keep improving that."
Category leadership. "we are the country's largest retail health insurer" (retail market share 29% this quarter).
Provider-network leverage: "We settled over 9.5 lakh claims during this quarter, of which more than 80% of claims were cashless through our network of hospitals."
margins & cost dynamics: CISR 98.7% → 97% (−1.7%), the fourth consecutive quarter of underwriting improvement; underwriting result Rs 111 crore vs Rs 16 crore.

Loss-ratio levers are deliberately un-attributed. COO: "it's a combined 360-degree approach... improving the portfolio quality, the pricing, and all the initiatives on claims starting from network management to wellness and... the teleconsultation piece." Asked repeatedly to quantify severity vs frequency vs FWA vs new-to-insurance mix, management declined to split.

Pricing cadence: annual, actuarially justified, product-by-product — "most of our pricing action of late has been in Q4 over the last couple of years"; the earned-premium impact then "plays out during the year". Forward pricing is "more like... a maintenance one. We do not believe in knee-jerk reactions."
Non-claimant discounts are being introduced alongside price action: "we will try to give benefits to non-claimants through some discounts which we are trying to bring in."

Reinsurance is a structural tailwind: the voluntary quota-share treaty of 2023-24 / 2024-25 ("a three-year treaty for long term business") is fading out; on the obligatory side "we are trying to negotiate with GICRE and we believe there should be some benefits coming out of it during the year." Net: "the reinsurance cost as a business will keep on coming down for us" — 0.9pp FY26 → 0.5-0.6% range.

Acquisition cost accounting clarified: employee expense is split three ways — claims-related into claims, sales-related into acquisition cost, support services into other expenses. Acquisition cost as a % of insurance revenue "has remained fairly stable".
Opex headwind: loss of GST input tax credit on operating expenses (tech/admin) drives the ~20% YoY rise in other expenses to Rs 283 crore.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No physical capex programme — the spend is technology and distribution:

ATOM Pro distribution app — "recognized by the Economic Times in the 'BFSI FinNext Awards 2026' under the 'InsurTech Product Excellence of the Year'"; 97% of new applications are now digitally sourced; an "always-on work stream continues to enhance the app capabilities."
Generative-AI claims layer in progress (no date, no quantified spend).
Agency expansion: ~20,000 agents added in the quarter → 8.5 lakh.
No commissioning dates, no capex number, no branch-count target was given — nothing to track for slippage this quarter.
capital allocation: Nothing disclosed on this call — no dividend, buyback, capital raise, solvency ratio or reinsurance-capital commentary beyond cost. The only capital-efficiency frame offered is the ROE glide path ("mid- to high-teen ROE") and the ROE-threshold discipline on underwriting: "We remained focused on disciplined and prudent risk selection in geographies, segments, channels and products that meet our defined ROE thresholds."
risks & watch-items: 1. Q2 FY27 vector-borne / infectious-disease season. "As we enter Quarter 2, we remain watchful of dengue, malaria, fever and infectious disease outbreaks"; "Q2 generally is a higher loss ratio for health insurance business... we expect the same trends to continue this year as well." COO says "we seem to be on track in terms of whatever we expected as outcomes."

2. GST-waiver base effect from H2 FY27. Management concedes "the growth rate optically may definitely moderate for everyone including for Star Health"; the mitigant offered is "the unwind of long-term policies" offsetting the high base — CEO agreed with that framing ("Yes, I think that's the right way to put it") but attached no number.
3. Market-share erosion, 31% → 29%. Partly reporting optics, partly deliberate — but a leader losing 2 points in a year in a fast-growing category is a live debate the call did not settle.

4. Loss-ratio improvement may be flattered by mix. ~100 bps improvement despite very strong fresh growth, D2C growth and price hikes prompted an analyst to ask whether "the loss ratio value on the back book is on an increasing trajectory". CEO's answer was directional only ("it is a work-in-progress all the time"), not a denial.

5. Impending regulatory action on commissions / distribution / claims. "we will await and see what the regulatory guidelines are and then we will be able to give you better clarity"; "we will not like to comment on what is the proposed regulation."

6. Disclosure gaps flagged by analysts on the call: no Schedule 6 reinsurance disclosure, no outstanding DAC number in the balance sheet ("What you give is only flow number"), and a contested classification of the Rs 38.8 crore insurance-contract finance income (analyst: should sit in investment, not underwriting; CFO deferred: "we can debate this in detail because it is quite technical").
7. No solvency ratio was given on the call — a standard SAHI disclosure absent from both prepared remarks and Q&A.
management quality / tone: Measured and unusually disciplined about not over-promising. The stand-out moment is CEO Anand Roy actively removing a guidance an analyst had inferred ("We are not giving any guidance for loss ratio improvement"), and declining an ROE number in favour of a directional glide path. The framing is consistently multi-quarter: "18 months ago, we set out on a course correction without recourse to short-term optical measures. FY26 demonstrated the result through a Rs 350 crore swing in Underwriting profit and this quarter's result is further evidence that this is being sustained." Growth is explicitly subordinated to quality — "We don't want to divert from that and chase growth for the sake of it." Two soft spots: repeated refusals to decompose the loss-ratio improvement into its drivers (fresh vs renewal, severity vs frequency vs FWA), and several technical questions (DAC, finance income, reinsurance run-rate) deflected to one-to-one follow-ups rather than answered on the call.
non-obvious takeaways: The senior-citizen identity is largely gone. Senior citizens are "hardly under 5% now of the overall book" — the loss-ratio improvement is as much a cohort re-mix into younger lives as it is pricing or claims discipline, and that lever is finite.

The group book has been shrunk by half in a year (~5% → ~2.5% of GWP). Reported blended loss ratio is now "more representative of the retail book" — meaning next year's YoY comparison loses this tailwind entirely.

The 1/N vs N split is not cosmetic. ~40% of fresh retail is long-term, revenue-recognised over 2-3 years. That is why 19% GWP growth prints as 13.4% insurance revenue growth — and it is also the built-in cushion management is counting on to absorb the H2 GST base effect.
Reinsurance is a quantified, near-certain margin tailwind hiding inside the expense line — 0.9pp (FY26) → 0.5-0.6% range — mechanical (treaty roll-off) rather than execution-dependent.

Regulatory reform is being positioned as an offensive weapon, not a risk. With 90% proprietary distribution and already-compliant EoM, a commission cap would asymmetrically hurt intermediary-dependent competitors: "we believe that we would be at an advantageous position in case of the reforms which comes in."
Renewal ratio above 100% (102%) means the existing book grows in premium terms before a single new policy is sold — the base on which the 20:80 fresh:renewal mix compounds.

Normalised PAT was introduced March'26 and reported PAT is now the higher number (Rs 550 cr vs Rs 386 cr). Management is voluntarily anchoring the market to the lower figure — the opposite of the usual adjusted-earnings direction.

Group cut to ~2.5% of GWP; senior citizens <5% of book; long-term ≈40% of fresh retail. Guidance given: insurance revenue growth 15-16% through FY27 and rising in FY28; expense ratio −30/40 bps p.a.; reinsurance cost 0.9pp → 0.5-0.6%. Guidance explicitly REFUSED: loss ratio, ROE number. Solvency ratio not disclosed on the call.

Q2 FY27 → check: (a) did the Q2 vector-borne season hold the loss ratio "on track" or break the four-quarter CISR streak; (b) did insurance revenue growth actually move 13.4% → 15-16%; (c) reinsurance expense trending to the 0.5-0.6% range and the GICRE obligatory negotiation outcome; (d) retail market share — 29% stabilising or eroding further; (e) whether the commission/distribution regulation landed and how; (f) whether a solvency ratio is disclosed.
